Div. 11, §§ 98.1101-98.1104)","requirement":"Proposed ordinance making it unlawful for a person to sell, license, or otherwise provide an algorithmic device to a landlord, and unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property. An 'algorithmic device' is software or a product that uses algorithms to perform calculations on nonpublic competitor data to advise or recommend rental rates or occupancy levels. Each month a landlord's use continues, and each residential rental property where it is used, is a separate violation. A tenant may sue a landlord for injunctive relief, damages, or civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation. A prevailing tenant recovers costs and reasonable attorney's fees, and lease clauses limiting fee recovery are unenforceable. Remedies are cumulative.
